name: The Scream
hook: Munch's howling figure is the world's most stolen masterpiece — and every clue is about the theft or the man.

facts.label: Edvard Munch
facts.statement: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter born in 1863 in Loten, Norway; he painted The Scream in 1893.

facts.label: The Scream
facts.statement: The Scream shows a figure with an open mouth against a red sky; experts concluded Munch wrote "Could only have been painted by a madman" on one version.

facts.label: Krakatoa
facts.statement: The red sky in The Scream may record debris in Oslo's air from the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa, halfway around the world.

facts.label: the art thefts
facts.statement: The Scream was stolen from Oslo's National Gallery in 1994, just before the Winter Olympics, and recovered three months later; the Munch Museum lost The Scream and Madonna in 2004.

facts.label: Oslo
facts.statement: Munch bequeathed his works to Oslo, where the Munch Museum displays them; a walking tour there visits his tomb.

facts.label: Expressionism
facts.statement: Munch was a pioneer of Expressionism, using color and line in a highly personal way to convey emotion.

facts.label: The Sick Child
facts.statement: Munch finished The Sick Child in 1886; after a 1908 breakdown he became more positive and painted murals for the University of Oslo.
